Commentary.Commentary: Back with the chase! The Indian players have walked out and are spreading to take their positions after a final huddle. Also, the two openers of the Sri Lankan Women stride out, where the skipper, Chamari Athapaththu, will open the innings alongside Hasini Perera. Kranti Gaud has the new ball in her hand, and she will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right, India Women walk into the break with a spring in their step. Sri Lanka Women? They need a revised DLS target of 271 runs in 47 overs, as per the host broadcasters. They’ve got the batters to chase, but after that sloppy fielding and losing grip at the death, can they really pull this off? Chase coming up…

Inoka Ranaweera is in for a chat. The Sri Lankan head coach, Rumesh Ratnayake, assists in translation. Inoka says that she stuck to her line and length and backed herself to do the job for the team. Shares that she did not start well but is happy with the way she executed later in the innings. Adds that she wanted to contain the runs and bowl defensively. Backs the batters to chase this total.

Sri Lanka’s bowling had firepower - Inoka was the standout with 4/46, showing why she’s their strike weapon. Udeshika Prabodhani’s new-ball spell was sharp, as she claimed two wickets, and even skipper Chamari chipped in. But those missed chances in the field were absolute killers, plus the discipline went missing in the last 2 overs, where they leaked 34 runs. From being on top at 124/6 to conceding 269/8, that’s a letdown they’ll regret.

But Deepti and Amanjot brought calm, grit, and then flair. They stitched a HUGE 103-run stand for the 7th wicket, the biggest partnership of the innings. Amanjot, riding her luck after multiple drops, made Sri Lanka pay with a gutsy half-century. Deepti matched her stroke for stroke, and both brought the fight back. Rain chopped the game down to 47 overs, but India turned that into an advantage, going full attack in the end overs. Rana’s late fireworks, including two towering sixes and two fours, sealed the momentum swing.

The innings began steadily but never fully settled. Smriti Mandhana fell early for just 8, not able to maintain her prolific opening stand with Pratika Rawal this time, and India managed 43/1 in the Powerplay before rain forced about a 75-minute break. Post-delay, Harleen Deol looked fluent, but Inoka Ranaweera flipped the script in one over - THREE wickets in five balls, sending Harleen, Jemimah, and skipper Harmanpreet packing. Add Richa Ghosh’s soft dismissal in the very next over, and India were reeling at 124/6. At that stage, even 200 looked like a dream.

What just happened? India were stumbling, rain was interrupting, wickets were tumbling… and still, they’ve posted 269/8 in 47 overs! Momentum? Oh yes, it’s all with them, thanks to the final two overs that exploded for 34 runs. Amanjot Kaur and Deepti Sharma were the saviours in a pressure-cooker situation, and with Sneh Rana smashing 28 unbeaten off just 15 at the end, India turned what looked like 250-ish into a commanding total. Sri Lanka? They’ll be kicking themselves for dropping Amanjot four times.

OUT! CAUGHT! Deepti Sharma holes out on the final ball! On the pads, on a length, Sharma brings her wrists into play and tries to whip it away aerially on the leg side. Hits it only as far as deep mid-wicket, where Sugandika Kumari runs across to her left and slides to take a fine catch. 18 runs and a wicket from the final over of the innings. India end up with 269 on the board!

Also, the playing conditions have been confirmed as per on-air, where the Powerplay will remain 10 overs long to start the Lankan innings. OUT! TAKEN! Udeshika Prabodhani has got the big fish, and Sri Lanka Women get the first breakthrough. This opening pair of Smriti Mandhana and Pratika Rawal has piled up massive partnerships, but not today, as Smriti departs for just 8 (10). Udeshika bowls it a bit fuller and keeps the line outside off, getting it to swing further away from the batter. Smriti takes a couple of steps forward and tries to loft it inside out over covers. But instead, she mistimes it off the toe end of the bat. The ball gets sliced towards deep point, where Vishmi Gunarathne moves forward, keeps her eyes on the ball and gets down on her knees to take the catch. Though the ball bobbles in her hands on the first attempt, she manages to take it on the second. A massive wicket for Sri Lanka Women, and they are all pumped up. India Women are 14/1.

Commentary.Commentary: With the national anthems complete, we are all set for the action to commence. When the players arrived at the ground, it was sunny, but clouds have rolled in since, prompting the floodlights to be switched on. There is a decent turnout for the first game of the tournament, with more expected to come in later in the evening. Chamari Athapaththu leads her troops out to the middle. They are followed by the two Indian openers, Smriti Mandhana and Pratika Rawal. Sri Lankan pacers will enjoy these overcast conditions. It will be the slingy right-arm quick, Achini Kulasuriya, to kickstart proceedings with the new ball for the island nation. Achini to Rawal with a slip in place. And away we go...

We are moments away from the first ball of the 13th edition of the ICC Women’s ODI World Cup. The tournament features an all-female officiating panel. First, the match officials will take the field, followed by the two sets of players. The giant flags have been laid out, and we are all set for the national anthems. Sri Lanka’s anthem will be sung first by Nuwandhika Senarathne, followed by the Indian national anthem, performed by Shreya Ghoshal.

Sri Lanka Women (Playing XI) - Chamari Athapaththu (C), Hasini Perera, Harshitha Samarawickrama, Vishmi Gunarathne, Kavisha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Anushka Sanjeewani (WK), Sugandika Kumari, Achini Kulasuriya, Udeshika Prabodhani, and Inoka Ranaweera.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Pratika Rawal, Harleen Deol, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Amanjot Kaur, Sneh Rana, Kranti Gaud, and Sree Charani.

The skipper of India, Harmanpreet Kaur, says that the team was also looking to bowl first, but stresses that the first game of a tournament is always important and they are treating it as a good opportunity. On the pitch, she feels it looks good and hopes her side can put a strong total on the board. Speaking about team combinations, she confirms that everyone is fit and they are going in with three spinners and two pacers. On Smriti Mandhana, she praises her as one of India’s best batters, recalling her brilliant form in recent series, and expresses confidence that she will continue that momentum into the World Cup. On the bigger picture, Harmanpreet says the team just wants to focus on playing good cricket, something they have been doing for the past few years, and continue in the same way throughout the tournament.

The captain of Sri Lanka, Chamari Athapaththu, says that this looks like a good batting track but expects the dew to arrive at night, which is why she has opted to bowl first. Informs that they are going with 7 batters and in terms of their bowling options, they have two off-spinners, two left-arm spinners and two pacers. Shares that they have had a good preparation through the domestic season and hopes to do well in this tournament with 5 out of their next 6 games being at home.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of Sri Lanka Women and their skipper, Chamari Athapaththu, has elected to FIELD first.
